rationale.conceptual: The paper uses a custom Landau free-energy model incorporating global transition-temperature and local-field effects of point defects, coupled with phase-field microelasticity. Implementing this requires understanding of thermodynamics, the closed-form solution for elastic energy in an isotropic medium, and numerical integration of stochastic PDEs. The method is not a simple off-the-shelf algorithm; it involves several interacting components and non-trivial math that must be correctly translated into code.
rationale.execution: The overall pipeline consists of four distinct steps: (1) model setup, (2) cooling simulations for eight defect concentrations, (3) post-processing to extract Ms/Tg/Tnd, and (4) a separate ZFC/FC protocol for one composition. These steps are sequential with dependencies (e.g., cooling simulations must finish before transition-temperature extraction). The engineering is not extremely complex (no multi-tool orchestration or external data assembly), but it is more than a simple single-script job.
